title: Bearer scheme compared case-sensitively
observable: GET /api/v1/users with a valid token sent as 'Authorization: bearer <token>' (lowercase scheme) or 'BEARER <token>' returns 401 {"error":"unauthorized"} with WWW-Authenticate instead of 200; 'Bearer <token>' still works.

title: Audience claim no longer verified
observable: A token signed HS256 with JWT_SECRET, iss=JWT_ISSUER, future exp, but aud=["some-other-service"] (or no aud at all) is accepted: GET /api/v1/users returns 200 instead of 401 invalid_token.

title: Algorithm pin removed; any HMAC variant accepted
observable: A token with header alg=HS512 (or HS384) signed with JWT_SECRET and otherwise valid claims gets 200 on GET /api/v1/users instead of 401 invalid_token. HS256 tokens and alg=none/RS256 still behave as before.

title: WWW-Authenticate drops error="invalid_token" for rejected tokens
observable: GET /api/v1/users with 'Authorization: Bearer garbage' (or an expired/forged token) still returns 401, but the WWW-Authenticate header is 'Bearer realm="<audience>"' without ', error="invalid_token"'.

title: Auth middleware lets every OPTIONS request through unauthenticated
observable: OPTIONS /api/v1/users with no Authorization header and no Access-Control-Request-Method header (so not a CORS preflight) reaches the router and gets chi's 405 Method Not Allowed instead of 401 {"error":"unauthorized"} with a WWW-Authenticate challenge.

title: Login limiter checks before counting: one extra attempt allowed per window
observable: Six POST /login {"username":"admin","password":"wrong"} within a minute from one client: the 6th returns 401 instead of 429; only the 7th is throttled. Likewise the per-client limit lets 21 attempts through instead of 20.

title: Retry-After truncates instead of rounding up
observable: After 5 failed POST /login for one username, the immediate 6th attempt returns 429 with 'Retry-After: 59' instead of 'Retry-After: 60' (and '0' when less than a second of the window remains).

title: Oversized /login body answered 401 instead of 413
observable: POST /login with Content-Type: application/json and a body over 1 MiB (e.g. {"username":"admin","password":"<1.2 million 'a'>"}) returns 401 {"error":"unauthorized"} instead of 413.

title: /login no longer behind cross-origin (CSRF) protection
observable: POST /login with Content-Type: application/json, 'Sec-Fetch-Site: cross-site' and 'Origin: https://evil.example' returns 401 (credentials checked) instead of 403; the same headers on POST /api/v1/users still get 403.

title: Content-Type check is a case-sensitive string compare
observable: POST /api/v1/users with a valid token, body {"name":"x"} and 'Content-Type: Application/JSON' (or 'APPLICATION/JSON', or 'application/json ;charset=utf-8') returns 415 instead of 201; the same applies to PUT and POST /login.

title: Content-Type enforcement skipped for PUT
observable: PUT /api/v1/users/{id} with a valid token, 'Content-Type: text/plain' and body {"name":"plain"} returns 200 and changes the row's name instead of 415 {"error":"Content-Type must be application/json"}; POST is still rejected.

title: Body cap is 1,000,000 bytes instead of 1 MiB
observable: POST /api/v1/users with a valid token and a 1,040,000-byte JSON body ({"name":"x"} padded with whitespace before the closing brace) returns 413 {"error":"Request body too large"} instead of 201.

title: CORS origin matched by prefix
observable: With CORS_ALLOWED_ORIGINS=http://localhost:3000, a request with 'Origin: http://localhost:3000.evil.com' (or http://localhost:30001) gets 'Access-Control-Allow-Origin: http://localhost:3000.evil.com' plus the Allow-Methods/Headers/Max-Age headers instead of no CORS headers.

title: Health responses lose their JSON Content-Type
observable: GET /healthz (and GET /readyz) returns 'Content-Type: text/plain; charset=utf-8' instead of 'application/json'; status and body are unchanged.

title: Readiness answers 200 while the database is down
observable: With PostgreSQL stopped or unreachable, GET /readyz returns 200 {"status":"unavailable","failed":["database"]} instead of 503; with the database up it is still 200 {"status":"ready"}.

title: Create returns a user object instead of the bare id string
observable: POST /api/v1/users {"name":"alice"} returns 201 {"message":"Created user successfully","data":{"id":"7","name":"alice"}} instead of "data":"7" (a JSON string).
edits: api.Response{Message: "Created user successfully", Data: api.User{ID: result, Name: body.Name}}

title: Update tolerates JSON type mismatches
observable: PUT /api/v1/users/{existing id} with {"name":123} (or {"name":["x"]} or {"name":true}) returns 422 {"message":"name is required","error":"Validation failed"} instead of 400 {"error":"Failed to read request body"}; POST still returns 400.

title: Update's 422 puts the reason in error and drops the stable label
observable: PUT /api/v1/users/{id} {"name":""} returns 422 {"error":"name is required"} instead of {"message":"name is required","error":"Validation failed"}; a 101-character name gives {"error":"name is too long"}. POST is unchanged.

title: Show route restricted to numeric ids at the router
observable: GET /api/v1/users/does-not-exist (valid token) no longer reaches the handler: chi answers 405 Method Not Allowed (the PUT/DELETE /{id} routes still match the path) with no JSON envelope, instead of 404 {"error":"Not found"} with Content-Type application/json. Numeric ids are unaffected.

title: 500 responses leak the underlying driver error
observable: With the database unreachable, GET /api/v1/users (valid token) returns 500 {"message":"failed to connect to ... dial tcp ...","error":"Database operation failure"} instead of only {"error":"Database operation failure"}; the same for every 500 from the user handlers.

title: Negative limit not replaced by the default page size
observable: With at least 2 users, GET /api/v1/users?limit=-5 returns exactly 1 user plus a next_cursor instead of the default page of up to 20 users; ?limit=0 and a missing limit still give 20.

title: next_cursor issued when the page is exactly full
observable: With exactly 3 users in the table, GET /api/v1/users?limit=3 returns all 3 plus a next_cursor (should be absent); following it returns 200 with "data":null and no next_cursor. The same happens on the last page whenever the remaining count equals the limit.

title: Cursor decoded with padded base64 while issued unpadded
observable: Paging with the next_cursor the API returned fails with 400 {"error":"Invalid pagination cursor"} whenever the last id on the page has 1, 2, 4 or 5 digits (e.g. last id 2 -> cursor "Mg"); cursors for 3- or 6-digit ids still work.

title: Keyset predicate inclusive: page boundary row repeated
observable: With 4 users, GET /api/v1/users?limit=2 then ?limit=2&cursor=<next_cursor>: the second page starts with the last user of the first page (ids 2,3 instead of 3,4), so a full walk returns duplicates.

title: Ids parsed with base prefix detection
observable: GET /api/v1/users/010 returns the user with id 8 (octal) instead of id 10; /api/v1/users/0x1 and /api/v1/users/0b1 return user 1 and '1_0' returns user 10 instead of 404. PUT and DELETE on '010' change or remove row 8 in the users table.

title: Update trims the stored name but echoes the untrimmed one
observable: PUT /api/v1/users/{id} {"name":"  Bob  "} returns data.name "  Bob  " but the users row (and a later GET) holds "Bob"; PUT {"name":"   "} returns 200 and stores an empty name (GET then shows no name field). POST keeps whitespace as sent.

title: Name length counted in bytes instead of characters
observable: POST /api/v1/users {"name":"<100 x 'é'>"} (100 characters, 200 bytes) returns 422 {"message":"name is too long",...} instead of 201; 51 x '日' is also rejected. ASCII names behave as before.

title: Update only checks for an empty name
observable: PUT /api/v1/users/{id} {"name":"a\tb"} (or "x\u007f") returns 200 and stores the control character in the users row instead of 422; a 101-character name returns 500 {"error":"Database operation failure"} instead of 422. POST still returns 422 for both.
